newsitem.title: UK: LME lists Sumitomo timeline in copper scandal.
newsitem.headline: LME lists Sumitomo timeline in copper scandal.

text.p: Key dates in the Sumitomo Corp coppper scandal as listed by the London Metal Exchange in a letter to the chairman of the U.S. House Banking Committee were as follows:

DECEMBER 5 1991 - LME Chief Executive David King notifies SIB of letter received form David Threlkeld concerning correspondence Threlkeld had received about seven weeks earlier from Sumitomo trader Yasuo Hamanaka.
DECEMBER 10 1991 - CEO and SIB officials meet in SIB offices with Hamanaka and another Sumitomo representative to discuss Threlkeld letter.
Neither LME nor SIB states that they accepted Hamanaka's explanation of its contents.
JANUARY 1992 - CEO meets with I Nishimumi, then Director and General Manager of the non-ferrous Metals Division of Sumitomo to discuss Sumitomo's activities in the copper market.
NOVEMBER 8 1995 - After being notified by LME CEO about his concerns over copper market developments, LME Board authorizes CEO to investigate various issues.

DECEMBER 1995 - After the most extensive and comprehensive investigation ever undertaken by the LME, the CEO seeks and receives approval to establish a sub-committee to continue the inquiry. A Board member not employed by an LME firm is appointed to avoid conflict of interest issues.

DECEMBER 1995-SPRING 1996 - The investigation continues with the SIB, SFA and CFTC being kept apprised of developments. The LME Board is not informed of the information gathered by the inquiry because its members are practitioners with conflicts of interests.
